title: What Zero-Waste Fashion Systems Is
definition: Zero-Waste Fashion Systems: fashion with no cutting waste.
description:
Strip Zero-Waste Fashion Systems to its essence and you get fashion with no cutting waste. Simple to say, civilizational to build.

The path runs through Future Art, Design & Fashion: first pattern algorithms understanding, then system logistics prototypes, then whole-garment knit operations at scale. Each stage has its own physics, its own economics, and its own failure modes — this database maps all three.

Use the ladder: start with foundations, work through the components and forecasts, run every demo, then attempt the compounded drills. By the final record you will hold a working mental model of system hulls, grounded in real research and honest about what remains unknown.

t: Real Research Today: Zero-Waste Fashion Systems
title: Real Research Today: Zero-Waste Fashion Systems
definition: Today's documented research behind Zero-Waste Fashion Systems.
description:
The road to Zero-Waste Fashion Systems is already being paved. 3D-printed fashion (Iris van Herpen) moves from runway to research labs. Algae-based textiles and dyes cut fashion's water and chemical footprint.

The Fashion for Good museum and Global Fashion Agenda push circular fashion. Together these programs form the pattern algorithms foundation that Zero-Waste Fashion Systems will build on — the system logistics results, the whole-garment knit methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as system logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Zero-Waste Fashion Systems
definition: Estimates Zero-Waste Fashion Systems readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Zero-Waste Fashion Systems components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a system hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Zero-Waste Fashion Systems Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Zero-Waste Fashion Systems: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Zero-Waste Fashion Systems — fashion with no cutting waste.

Phase 1 — Prove (pattern algorithms): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (system logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (whole-garment knit): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (take-back): system hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and fashion-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
